title: Marbury v. Madison
author: John Marshall
summary: Held that the Supreme Court can strike down laws that conflict with the Constitution.
impact: Established judicial review, the Court's most important power.

title: McCulloch v. Maryland
author: John Marshall
summary: Upheld Congress's power to create a national bank and barred states from taxing it.
impact: Established broad 'implied powers' for the federal government, the basis for most economic legislation since.

title: Dartmouth College v. Woodward
author: John Marshall
summary: Held that a state could not rewrite a private college's charter, because charters are contracts protected by the Constitution.
impact: Protected corporations from state interference and helped private business grow.

title: Gibbons v. Ogden
author: John Marshall
summary: Held that Congress's power over interstate commerce overrides a state-granted steamboat monopoly.
impact: Opened the door to broad federal regulation of the national economy.

title: Worcester v. Georgia
author: John Marshall
summary: Held that Georgia had no authority over Cherokee land; only the federal government could deal with the Cherokee Nation.
impact: Andrew Jackson and Georgia ignored it, and the Cherokee were forcibly removed on the Trail of Tears.

title: Barron v. Baltimore
author: John Marshall
summary: Held that the Bill of Rights limits only the federal government, not the states.
impact: States were free to ignore the Bill of Rights until the 14th Amendment and 20th-century rulings applied it to them.

title: Prigg v. Pennsylvania
author: Joseph Story
summary: Struck down a Pennsylvania law that protected free Black people from being kidnapped into slavery, holding that the federal Fugitive Slave Act came first.
impact: Northern states responded by refusing to help enforce it, which led to the harsher Fugitive Slave Act of 1850.

title: Dred Scott v. Sandford
author: Roger Brooke Taney
summary: Held that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories.
impact: Widely considered the worst decision in the Court's history; overturned by the 13th and 14th Amendments.

title: Ex parte Milligan
author: David Davis
summary: Held that civilians cannot be tried by military courts where regular courts are open, even in wartime.
impact: Limited Lincoln's wartime arrests after the fact and remains a key check on military power over civilians.

title: Hepburn v. Griswold
author: Salmon Portland Chase
summary: Struck down the Civil War law making paper 'greenbacks' legal tender for debts made before it passed.
impact: Reversed only 15 months later after two new justices joined.

title: Legal Tender Cases (Knox v. Lee)
author: William Strong
summary: Upheld paper money as legal tender for all debts, reversing Hepburn v. Griswold.
impact: Confirmed the federal government's power to issue paper currency.

title: Slaughter-House Cases
author: Samuel Freeman Miller
summary: Upheld a Louisiana law regulating slaughterhouses and read the 14th Amendment's 'privileges or immunities' clause very narrowly.
impact: Allowed state economic regulation but crippled one of the main tools meant to protect freed people's rights.

title: United States v. Cruikshank
author: Morrison Remick Waite
summary: Overturned the convictions of white men involved in the Colfax massacre of Black citizens, holding that the Bill of Rights and 14th Amendment did not let the federal government punish private violence.
impact: Left Black Southerners largely unprotected from white terror groups.

title: Munn v. Illinois
author: Morrison Remick Waite
summary: Upheld state regulation of grain elevator rates, because businesses 'affected with a public interest' can be regulated.
impact: Laid the groundwork for regulating railroads and utilities.

title: Civil Rights Cases
author: Joseph P. Bradley
summary: Struck down the Civil Rights Act of 1875's ban on racial discrimination in hotels, theaters and railroads, holding the 14th Amendment reached only government action.
impact: Cleared the way for private segregation until the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

title: Yick Wo v. Hopkins
author: Stanley Matthews
summary: Struck down a San Francisco laundry ordinance enforced only against Chinese owners, holding that a fair law applied unfairly violates equal protection.
impact: One of the first rulings to protect noncitizens under the 14th Amendment.

title: United States v. E.C. Knight Co.
author: Melville Weston Fuller
summary: Held that the Sherman Antitrust Act did not reach a sugar refining monopoly, because manufacturing is not commerce.
impact: Weakened antitrust enforcement for a decade.

title: Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co.
author: Melville Weston Fuller
summary: Struck down the federal income tax of 1894 as an unconstitutional direct tax.
impact: Blocked a federal income tax until the 16th Amendment in 1913.

title: In re Debs
author: David Josiah Brewer
summary: Upheld the federal injunction used to break the Pullman railroad strike and the contempt conviction of union leader Eugene Debs.
impact: Made court injunctions a powerful weapon against strikes until Congress limited them in 1932.

title: Plessy v. Ferguson
author: Henry Billings Brown
summary: Upheld racial segregation on railroad cars under the doctrine of 'separate but equal'.
impact: Gave legal cover to Jim Crow segregation for nearly 60 years.

title: United States v. Wong Kim Ark
author: Horace Gray
summary: Held that a man born in San Francisco to Chinese parents was a U.S. citizen under the 14th Amendment.
impact: Confirmed birthright citizenship for nearly everyone born on U.S. soil.

title: Lochner v. New York
author: Rufus Wheeler Peckham
summary: Struck down a New York law limiting bakers to 60 hours a week as a violation of 'liberty of contract'.
impact: Began a 30-year era in which the Court struck down many labor laws.

title: Muller v. Oregon
author: David Josiah Brewer
summary: Upheld a 10-hour workday limit for women, relying on a brief by Louis Brandeis full of social science.
impact: Allowed some labor protections despite Lochner, though its reasoning rested on ideas about women's weakness.

title: Hammer v. Dagenhart
author: William Rufus Day
summary: Struck down the federal ban on shipping goods made with child labor across state lines.
impact: Delayed a national child labor ban until 1938.

title: Schenck v. United States
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
summary: Upheld the conviction of a Socialist who mailed anti-draft leaflets, creating the 'clear and present danger' test.
impact: Allowed wartime prosecution of speech; later narrowed by Brandenburg v. Ohio.

title: Adkins v. Children's Hospital
author: George Sutherland
summary: Struck down a minimum wage for women in Washington, D.C., as a violation of liberty of contract.
impact: Blocked minimum wage laws until 1937.

title: Buck v. Bell
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
summary: Upheld Virginia's forced sterilization of people deemed 'unfit'.
impact: About 60,000 Americans were sterilized under such laws. Never formally overruled.

title: Gold Clause Cases (Norman v. B&O Railroad)
author: Charles Evans Hughes
summary: Upheld Congress's cancellation of contract clauses requiring payment in gold.
impact: Let the government devalue the dollar and pay debts in paper money.

title: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States
author: Charles Evans Hughes
summary: Unanimously struck down the National Industrial Recovery Act for giving too much lawmaking power to the president and reaching local business.
impact: Ended the NRA, the centerpiece of the early New Deal.

title: United States v. Butler
author: Owen Josephus Roberts
summary: Struck down the Agricultural Adjustment Act's tax on food processors used to pay farmers to cut production.
impact: Forced a rewrite of New Deal farm policy, though it read Congress's spending power broadly.

title: West Coast Hotel Co. v. Parrish
author: Charles Evans Hughes
summary: Upheld Washington State's minimum wage for women, overruling Adkins.
impact: Ended the Lochner era; came weeks after Roosevelt's court-packing plan and is often called 'the switch in time that saved nine'.

title: Helvering v. Davis
author: Benjamin Nathan Cardozo
summary: Upheld Social Security's old-age benefits as a valid use of Congress's power to tax and spend for the general welfare.
impact: Secured the constitutional basis of Social Security.

title: United States v. Darby
author: Harlan Fiske Stone
summary: Upheld the Fair Labor Standards Act's minimum wage, overtime and child labor rules.
impact: Overruled Hammer v. Dagenhart and settled Congress's power to set national labor standards.

title: Wickard v. Filburn
author: Robert H. Jackson
summary: Held that Congress could limit wheat a farmer grew for his own use, because such activity together affects interstate commerce.
impact: The high-water mark of federal commerce power.

title: Korematsu v. United States
author: Hugo L. Black
summary: Upheld the wartime exclusion of Japanese Americans from the West Coast.
impact: The Court repudiated it in 2018; Congress apologized and paid reparations in 1988.

title: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
author: Hugo L. Black
summary: Held that President Truman could not seize the steel mills without authority from Congress.
impact: Justice Jackson's concurrence became the standard test for limits on presidential power.

title: Brown v. Board of Education
author: Earl Warren
summary: Unanimously held that segregated public schools are unconstitutional.
impact: Overruled Plessy v. Ferguson and launched the end of legal segregation.

title: Mapp v. Ohio
author: Tom C. Clark
summary: Held that evidence from illegal searches cannot be used in state criminal trials.
impact: Applied the 'exclusionary rule' to every police department in the country.

title: Baker v. Carr
author: William J. Brennan, Jr.
summary: Held that federal courts can hear challenges to unequal legislative districts.
impact: Led to 'one person, one vote' and the redrawing of nearly every legislature in the country.

title: Engel v. Vitale
author: Hugo L. Black
summary: Held that official prayer in public schools violates the ban on establishing religion.
impact: Ended state-sponsored school prayer.

title: Gideon v. Wainwright
author: Hugo L. Black
summary: Unanimously held that states must provide a lawyer to criminal defendants who cannot afford one.
impact: Created the modern public defender system.

title: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan
author: William J. Brennan, Jr.
summary: Held that public officials must prove 'actual malice' to win a libel suit.
impact: Protected the press, including civil rights coverage in the South, from ruinous lawsuits.

title: Heart of Atlanta Motel v. United States
author: Tom C. Clark
summary: Unanimously upheld the Civil Rights Act of 1964's ban on discrimination in hotels under Congress's commerce power.
impact: Secured the Civil Rights Act's reach over private businesses.

title: Griswold v. Connecticut
author: William O. Douglas
summary: Struck down a ban on contraceptives for married couples, recognizing a constitutional right to privacy.
impact: The foundation for later rulings on abortion and intimate relationships.

title: Miranda v. Arizona
author: Earl Warren
summary: Held that police must warn suspects of their right to remain silent and to a lawyer before questioning.
impact: Created the 'Miranda warnings' read in every arrest.

title: Loving v. Virginia
author: Earl Warren
summary: Unanimously struck down laws banning interracial marriage.
impact: Ended such bans in 16 states.

title: Tinker v. Des Moines
author: Abe Fortas
summary: Held that students who wore black armbands to protest the Vietnam War were protected by free speech.
impact: Students do not 'shed their constitutional rights … at the schoolhouse gate'.

title: Brandenburg v. Ohio
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Overturned a Ku Klux Klan leader's conviction, holding that speech can be punished only if it incites imminent lawless action.
impact: The modern test protecting even hateful political speech.

title: New York Times Co. v. United States (Pentagon Papers)
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Let newspapers publish the leaked Pentagon Papers, rejecting the Nixon administration's request to block them.
impact: A landmark against government censorship of the press.

title: Furman v. Georgia
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Held that the death penalty as then applied was arbitrary and unconstitutional.
impact: Halted executions nationwide until states rewrote their laws.

title: Roe v. Wade
author: Harry A. Blackmun
summary: Recognized a constitutional right to abortion, with limits increasing later in pregnancy.
impact: Legalized abortion nationwide for 49 years.

title: United States v. Nixon
author: Warren E. Burger
summary: Unanimously ordered President Nixon to turn over the Watergate tapes, rejecting an absolute executive privilege.
impact: Nixon resigned 16 days later.

title: Buckley v. Valeo
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Upheld limits on campaign contributions but struck down limits on campaign spending as limits on speech.
impact: Set the framework for campaign finance law.

title: Gregg v. Georgia
author: Potter Stewart
summary: Upheld Georgia's rewritten death penalty law.
impact: Allowed executions to resume in 1977.

title: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
author: Lewis F. Powell, Jr.
summary: Struck down a medical school's racial quota but allowed race to be one factor in admissions.
impact: Governed affirmative action in college admissions for 45 years.

title: Chevron U.S.A. v. NRDC
author: John Paul Stevens
summary: Held that courts should defer to a federal agency's reasonable reading of an unclear law.
impact: Became one of the most-cited rulings in administrative law.

title: Bowsher v. Synar
author: Warren E. Burger
summary: Struck down the automatic spending-cut trigger in the Gramm–Rudman–Hollings deficit law, because it gave executive power to an officer Congress controls.
impact: Congress rewrote the trigger in 1987.

title: Texas v. Johnson
author: William J. Brennan, Jr.
summary: Held that burning the American flag in protest is protected speech.
impact: Struck down flag-desecration laws in 48 states.

title: Planned Parenthood v. Casey
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Reaffirmed the core of Roe v. Wade while letting states add restrictions that do not place an 'undue burden' on abortion.
impact: Governed abortion law for 30 years.

title: United States v. Lopez
author: William H. Rehnquist
summary: Struck down a federal ban on guns near schools as beyond Congress's commerce power.
impact: The first limit on the commerce power in nearly 60 years.

title: Clinton v. City of New York
author: John Paul Stevens
summary: Struck down the line-item veto, which let the president cancel individual spending items after signing a bill.
impact: The president must sign or veto a bill as a whole.

title: Bush v. Gore
author: Unsigned (per curiam) or plurality
summary: Stopped the Florida recount in the 2000 presidential election.
impact: George W. Bush won Florida by 537 votes and the presidency.

title: Lawrence v. Texas
author: Anthony M. Kennedy
summary: Struck down laws criminalizing gay sex.
impact: Overruled Bowers v. Hardwick (1986) and paved the way for marriage equality.

title: Kelo v. City of New London
author: John Paul Stevens
summary: Allowed a city to take private homes for a private economic development project as a 'public use'.
impact: Widely unpopular on both left and right; more than 40 states passed laws limiting such takings.

title: District of Columbia v. Heller
author: Antonin Scalia
summary: Held that the Second Amendment protects an individual right to keep a handgun at home for self-defense.
impact: The first ruling to strike down a gun law under the Second Amendment.

title: Citizens United v. FEC
author: Anthony M. Kennedy
summary: Held that corporations and unions can spend unlimited amounts on independent political ads.
impact: Led to super PACs and a surge in outside election spending.

title: NFIB v. Sebelius
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Upheld the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate as a tax, but let states opt out of the Medicaid expansion.
impact: Saved the ACA; about 10 states still have not expanded Medicaid.

title: Shelby County v. Holder
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Struck down the formula deciding which states needed federal approval to change voting rules under the Voting Rights Act.
impact: Ended federal 'preclearance' of election changes in mostly Southern states.

title: King v. Burwell
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Upheld Affordable Care Act subsidies for people in every state, including those using the federal exchange.
impact: Kept health insurance subsidies for about 6 million people.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges
author: Anthony M. Kennedy
summary: Held that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry.
impact: Legalized same-sex marriage nationwide.

title: Bostock v. Clayton County
author: Neil M. Gorsuch
summary: Held that the Civil Rights Act's ban on sex discrimination in employment covers gay and transgender workers.
impact: Extended federal job protections nationwide; written by Trump appointee Neil Gorsuch.

title: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
author: Samuel A. Alito, Jr.
summary: Overruled Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey, holding that the Constitution does not protect a right to abortion.
impact: Returned abortion law to the states; more than a dozen banned most abortions.

title: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen
author: Clarence Thomas
summary: Struck down New York's limits on carrying handguns in public and required gun laws to fit the nation's historical tradition.
impact: Led courts to review gun laws nationwide under the new history test.

title: Biden v. Nebraska
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Struck down the Biden administration's plan to cancel up to $20,000 in student loans per borrower.
impact: Blocked about $400 billion in loan forgiveness.

title: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Held that race-conscious college admissions violate equal protection.
impact: Ended affirmative action in college admissions.

title: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Overruled Chevron, holding that courts, not agencies, decide what unclear laws mean.
impact: Opened thousands of federal regulations to new court challenges.

title: Trump v. United States
author: John G. Roberts, Jr.
summary: Held that former presidents have absolute immunity from prosecution for core constitutional acts and presumptive immunity for other official acts.
impact: Delayed and narrowed the federal case over Donald Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election.
